# Newlib 3.3.0 formatter candidate

Unmodified selected source at commit `6d79e0a58866548f435527798fbd4a6849d05bc7`, the Newlib revision named by the cached GNU Arm Embedded 9-2020-q2-update release notes. `provenance.json` records primary-source byte verification for snprintf/vfprintf and mirror archive byte verification for every selected file. Full primary closure verification remains gated after HTTP 429. This distribution includes software developed by the University of California, Berkeley. See retained file notices and the complete `COPYING.NEWLIB` license bundle; no upstream endorsement is implied.

Build with `/tmp/r1-source-venv/bin/python r1/tools/build_newlib_stdio.py` from the repository root. Installed Newlib configuration and public headers are hash-bound in the report, along with every private header. `STRING_ONLY` retains floating-point formatting; the integer variant additionally supplies the shared string stream output helper. No upstream code has been changed, including the compiler warning in `mprec.c`.

The relocatable output is a partial source candidate. Its report retains four unresolved assertion, allocator-lock and heap-growth boundaries. The compiler-rt EABI adapters and existing integer/memory providers are linked by hash-bound receipts. Source compilation establishes neither original Newlib attribution for the stock firmware nor behavioral, ABI, instruction or whole-image identity. A bounded native experiment has 139 matches and 86 counterexamples across 225 cases, with no execution errors. Pointer spelling, unsupported native %a and extreme floating values prevent generic admission. Native reconstruction and complete helper closure remain required. Pin upgrades must regenerate provenance/build receipts and repeat native comparisons before admission; this pin does not automatically follow upstream changes.
